guide_line: Compare radius, ionization energy, and electron affinity, and watch the Be, N, and Mg exceptions.
steps: Atomic radius grows down a group because n gets larger. Across a period, radius shrinks because the nucleus pulls harder on the same shell.
A cation is smaller than its atom. An anion is larger than its atom. When ions have the same number of electrons, more protons means a smaller ion.

Ionization energy is the energy needed to remove an electron. It mostly rises across a period and falls down a group. Remember the exceptions: Be is higher than B, N is higher than O, and Mg is higher than Al.

A big jump in successive ionization energies means the next electron comes from a full inner shell. Two or fewer easy electrons gives group 1 or 2. More than two easy electrons gives a group whose ones digit matches that count.

Electron affinity is the energy change when a gas atom gains an electron. A negative value means energy is released. Halogens release energy. A noble gas does not follow that trend, because the next electron would start a new shell.
Electronegativity rises toward fluorine. Metallic character rises toward cesium. Chlorine releases more energy than fluorine when it gains one electron.

worked_example.q: Which atom has the largest radius: Li, Be, or B? Write the element symbol.
steps: Li, Be, and B are in the same period.
Radius shrinks from left to right, so Li is the largest.

similar_problem.q: Which atom has the highest ionization energy: N, O, or F? Write the element symbol.
similar_problem.hint: In period 2 the general rise points to the right, and the N-versus-O exception still leaves F highest.

problems.q: Which atom has the largest radius: Na, Mg, or Al? Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: Na, Mg, and Al are in period 3. Radius shrinks across a period, so Na is the largest.
hints: These three are in one period. Pick the one farthest left.

problems.q: Which atom has the smallest radius: F, Cl, or Br? Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: F, Cl, and Br are in group 17. Radius grows down a group, so F is the smallest.
hints: These three are in one group. The top atom has the smallest n.

problems.q: Rank Cl, Si, Mg, and Na from smallest radius to largest. Separate the symbols with <, with spaces around the sign.
problems.why: All four are in period 3. Radius shrinks as atomic number rises, so Cl < Si < Mg < Na.
hints: Stay in period 3 and put the rightmost atom first.

problems.q: Which is larger, a K atom or a K+ ion? Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He. Type K or K+.
problems.why: K+ has lost the 4s electron, so it has one fewer shell than the K atom. The atom is larger.
hints: The positive ion lost the outer electron. Compare the atom with that ion.

problems.q: Which is larger, an S atom or an S2- ion? Type S or S2-.
problems.why: S2- has two extra electrons in the same shell and more repulsion, so the ion is larger than the atom.
hints: Adding electrons to make the anion spreads the cloud out.

problems.q: Rank these ions from smallest to largest: Na+, Mg2+, O2-, F-. They all have 10 electrons. Separate the ions with < and put spaces around the sign.
problems.why: Same electron count: more protons pull harder. Proton counts are Mg 12, Na 11, F 9, O 8, so Mg2+ < Na+ < F- < O2-.
hints: Line the four ions up by the number of protons. The most protons make the smallest ion.

problems.q: Which atom has the higher first ionization energy, Mg or Al? Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: Al starts a 3p electron, which is easier to remove than a paired electron from Mg's full 3s. Mg is higher.
hints: This is the period-3 exception. The new p electron is easier to remove than the full s pair.

problems.q: Which atom has the higher first ionization energy, N or O? Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: Oxygen's fourth 2p electron is paired. That pair is easier to remove than one of nitrogen's three unpaired 2p electrons. N is higher.
hints: This is the period-2 exception just before oxygen. The half-full 2p subshell is harder to break.

problems.q: Which atom has the highest first ionization energy: N, O, or F? Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: F is farthest right. The N > O exception does not put N above F.
hints: Move toward the right side of period 2. The exception is only between N and O.

problems.q: A period-4 atom has these successive ionization energies, in kJ/mol, rounded: 520, 1400, 18000, 21000. What is its group number? Type the number only.
problems.why: The first jump that more than triples is from 1400 to 18000, after two electrons. Two easy electrons means group 2.
hints: Find the first energy that is more than triple the one before it in 520, 1400, 18000, 21000.

problems.q: An atom has these successive ionization energies, in kJ/mol, rounded: 1100, 2400, 4600, 6200, 38000. What is its group number? Type the number only.
problems.why: The big jump is from 6200 to 38000, after four electrons. Four easy electrons means group 14.
hints: In 1100, 2400, 4600, 6200, 38000, count the energies before the jump that more than triples, then add 10.

problems.q: An atom has these successive ionization energies, in kJ/mol, rounded: 500, 4600, 6900. What is its group number? Type the number only.
problems.why: The jump from 500 to 4600 comes after one electron. One easy electron means group 1.
hints: The first gap in 500, 4600, 6900 is already more than triple. Count only the energies before it.

problems.q: Which is more metallic, Ca or Ge? Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: Metallic character falls across a period. Ca is left of Ge, so Ca is more metallic.
hints: Pick the atom farther toward the lower left. Ge is on the staircase.

problems.q: Which atom has the higher electronegativity, S or Cl? Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: Electronegativity rises across a period toward fluorine. Cl is right of S.
hints: In period 3, the atom closer to fluorine holds bonding electrons more tightly.

problems.q: Which atom releases more energy when it gains one electron, F or Cl? Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: Chlorine's added electron goes into a roomier n = 3 shell, so Cl releases more energy than F.
hints: This pair breaks the simple left-to-right pattern. Compare the shell the new electron enters.

problems.q: Which ion is larger, Ca2+ or K+? Type Ca2+ or K+.
problems.why: Both ions have 18 electrons. Ca has 20 protons and K has 19, so K+ is larger.
hints: The electron count is the same. The ion with fewer protons is larger.

problems.q: Which atom has the higher effective nuclear charge felt by its valence electrons, Na or Cl? Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: Across period 3 the nucleus has more protons while the valence shell stays n = 3. Cl feels the higher pull.
hints: Compare atoms in the same period. More protons with the same n means a stronger pull.

problems.q: Rank K, Na, and Li by increasing first ionization energy. Separate the symbols with <, with spaces around the sign.
problems.why: Ionization energy falls down group 1, so the increasing order is K < Na < Li.
hints: Put the bottom of group 1 first. The smallest atom holds its electron hardest.

problems.q: Which atom loses one electron more easily, Sr or Br? Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: Sr is a group 2 metal and Br is a halogen. The metal's outer electron is easier to remove.
hints: The metal is on the left. A low ionization energy means the electron leaves more easily.

problems.q: Which atom has the higher first ionization energy, Be or B? Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: Boron starts a 2p electron. That electron is easier to remove than one from beryllium's full 2s. Be is higher.
hints: This is the period-2 exception at the start of the p block. A full 2s holds its electrons more tightly than the new 2p electron.

problems.q: Rank N, P, and As by increasing atomic radius. Separate the symbols with <, with spaces around the sign.
problems.why: N, P, and As are in group 15. Radius grows as n grows, so N < P < As.
hints: Stay in one group and put the top of the group first. The shell number increases down the column.

problems.q: A chlorine atom releases energy when it gains one electron. Is the electron affinity of chlorine positive or negative? Type positive or negative.
problems.why: Energy leaving the atom is a negative energy change. Chlorine's electron affinity is negative.
hints: Released energy is written with a negative sign. Chlorine does release energy when the electron is added.

problems.q: Which atom has the more favorable electron affinity, Br or Kr? Write the element symbol with a capital letter, like He.
problems.why: Bromine can place the new electron in 4p. Krypton already has a full shell, so the next electron would start 5s. Br is more favorable.
hints: A halogen can finish its p subshell. A noble gas cannot take an electron into the same shell.
